## Collectives and global decisions {#sec-ch14-collectives}

### Summary

When a run is split over several processes, a few decisions must come out the same on every one of them: the
length of the next time step, whether to redo a step, and whether to stop on a signal. If two processes disagreed,
their blocks would no longer advance together. This section lists the global reductions that make those decisions,
what each one combines, and which of them give the same result on any number of processes.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**Purpose.** Makes the decisions every rank must share (time step, redo, stop) identical on every process.

**Data.** Small host tensors: the local stable step, six redo flags, the signal count, the fixer sums.

**Placement.** Once per step in `MeshImpl` (`max_time_step`, `check_redo`) and at output and finalisation.

**Activation.** Always with more than one process; no option. One process reduces nothing.

**Guarantee / limits.** MIN and MAX are exact and order free; the fixer SUM is order dependent, bounded below.

**Evidence.** The Tests layer below, @tbl-ch14-collectives-tests.
:::

Local symbols: $n_{\mathrm{redo}}$ the redo count of the current step [count];
$N$ the number of terms of a sum [count] and $b_k$ its terms; $C$[^rg-9793b59d7bc0] the Courant number, `cfl`[^rg-fe505223b66c] [-], $\Theta$[^rg-abef336e38dd] the
limiter's donor factor [-] and $\epsilon_{\mathrm m}$[^rg-6f5d38ae36e6] the machine epsilon, all three defined in @sec-appa.

| decision | reduction | tensor | where |
|---|---|---|---|
| time step | MIN of the local stable step | 1 double | `MeshImpl::max_time_step` |
| redo | MAX of 6 cause flags | 6 doubles (0 or 1) | `reduce_redo_flags` |
| stop on a signal | MAX of the caught-signal count | 1 int32 | `SignalHandler::CheckSignalFlags` |
| gravity-work fixer | SUM of 5 sums | 5 doubles | `MeshImpl::forward`; see below |
| cycle line: totals, energies and meters | SUM, MIN of $\Theta$, MAX of the VIC[^rg-0726addd7156] residual, to the root | small doubles | `print_cycle_diagnostics` |
| cell count for the timing line | SUM to the root | 1 int64 | `MeshBlockImpl::finalize` |

: The collectives of one run. {#tbl-ch14-collectives}

Barriers sit at initialisation, around every combined output (@sec-ch14-netcdf, @sec-ch14-restart) and at
finalisation.

### Derivation

Why every rank takes the same decision, in four steps:

1. *A MIN or MAX returns one of its inputs.* The minimum of doubles is computed by comparisons only, with no
   arithmetic, so it is exact and equal to one of the values reduced.
2. *That input does not depend on the order.* The minimum of a finite set is the same set element whatever order the
   backend combines the values in. So every rank receives the same bits whatever the process count or backend.
3. *The decisions use MIN or MAX only.* The time step is a MIN (`MeshImpl::max_time_step`), the redo causes and the
   signal count are MAX (`reduce_redo_flags`, `CheckSignalFlags`). So every rank takes the same step, the same redo
   decision and the same stop.
4. *A SUM is different.* A floating-point sum of $N$ terms $b_k$, combined in any order or tree, differs from the exact
   sum by at most $(N-1)\,\tfrac12\epsilon_{\mathrm m}\sum_k\lvert b_k\rvert$: each of its $N-1$ additions rounds a
   partial sum bounded by $\sum_k\lvert b_k\rvert$ with relative error at most $\tfrac12\epsilon_{\mathrm m}=2^{-53}$,
   as in the round-off bound of @sec-ch09-framework. Two orders can differ by twice that. The gravity-work fixer SUM
   is the one SUM that feeds the state (@sec-ch14-repro).

`[C14]` of `derivation_check.py` confirms steps 1 and 2 over all 720 orders of six doubles, and `[C15]` the bound of
step 4 on 300 random summation trees.

### Numerical method

**Time step.** `MeshImpl::max_time_step` takes the minimum of `local_max_time_step` over the local blocks on the
host, all-reduces it with MIN and returns $2^{-n_{\mathrm{redo}}}\,C\,\Delta t$, with $n_{\mathrm{redo}}$ the current redo
count and $C$ the CFL[^rg-e0adecef2ed5] number ({{< code src/mesh/mesh.cpp MeshImpl::max_time_step >}}). The single-block path does the same per block
(`MeshBlockImpl::max_time_step`, {{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::max_time_step >}}).

**Redo.** `MeshImpl::check_redo` first checks signals. Each local block then forms its six flags as one float64
tensor on its device: density or pressure floor hit, VIC dry clamp, the two limiter marks, saturation-adjustment
failure and implicit solve failure. A seventh entry carries the vapour-repair failures counted during
the step (`local_redo_flag_tensor`,
{{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::local_redo_flag_tensor >}}). When the local blocks share a device,
the mesh stacks the tensors, takes their element-wise maximum on the device and reads it to the host once;
otherwise it reads each block's tensor and ORs them. The read sets the limiter flag when the seventh
entry is set, and returns the six flags (`read_redo_flags`,
{{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::read_redo_flags >}}; {{< code src/mesh/mesh.cpp MeshImpl::check_redo >}}).
`reduce_redo_flags` all-reduces the six values with MAX and packs the result into a cause bit mask
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::reduce_redo_flags >}}).
Every block on every process then applies the same decision: a hit anywhere rolls back every block
(`MeshImpl::check_redo`, {{< code src/mesh/mesh.cpp MeshImpl::check_redo >}}). The redo itself is the subject of @sec-ch07-redo.

**Signals.** SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGALRM set flags. `CheckSignalFlags` sums the local flags with the signals blocked,
all-reduces the count with MAX, and returns it; a non-zero value makes `check_redo` return $-1$ and the driver stop.
With no snapy process group it falls back to a registered external group
(`CheckSignalFlags`, {{< code src/utils/signal_handler.cpp SignalHandler::CheckSignalFlags >}}).

**Cycle line.** On every cycle that prints a line (each `ncycle_out`[^rg-9751aed7d553]-th), `print_cycle_diagnostics` reduces the
conserved totals, the kinetic and potential energies and the
limiter meters with SUM, the smallest $\Theta$ with MIN and the VIC clamp residual with MAX, each a `reduce` to the
root process, which prints them ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp print_cycle_diagnostics >}}, `reduce`). These sums are printed
only; nothing in the state depends on them.

**Gravity-work fixer.**

The fixer runs only with `gravity-work: cell`, which is not the default (`face` is), so a default run makes no
fixer reduction (@sec-ch13-fixgrav). When it runs, after the last stage of each step every block forms five
float64 numbers on the host in `gravity_work_fixer_sums` ({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::gravity_work_fixer_sums >}}):
the stage-weighted $E_{\mathrm{tot}}+\mathrm{PE}_d$ defect, the fluid mass, the mass through the $x_1$ boundary faces, the mass of
the wall cells and a redo flag. Each is itself a sum over the block's cells, formed by torch on the block's device.
With one block per process the block all-reduces its vector with SUM directly
(`gravity_work_fixer_sums`, {{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::advance_local >}}). With several local blocks,
`MeshImpl::forward` sets `defer_gravity_work_fixer` on every block, adds the blocks' vectors into a zero vector in
block index order, $0,1,\dots$, and makes one allreduce SUM for the process
(`gravity_work_fixer_sums`, {{< code src/mesh/mesh.cpp MeshImpl::forward >}}). The order in which the allreduce adds the
processes' vectors is the backend's; the code does not fix it. Every block then applies the same reduced vector.

**Barriers.** `initialize` holds all processes at a barrier before the first step
({{< code src/mesh/meshblock.cpp MeshBlockImpl::initialize >}}); the combines of NetCDF and restart files each have
a barrier and a mirror barrier; `finalize` ends with a barrier and, if snapy owns the group, a shutdown
(`MeshImpl::finalize`, {{< code src/mesh/mesh.cpp MeshImpl::finalize >}}).

### Code

**A minimal input.** None: the reductions have no option. They run whenever the launch implies more than one
process (@sec-ch14-launch), and a single process skips every collective (`has_process_group` is false).

**What is refused, and why.** Nothing is refused here. A rank that never reaches a collective leaves the others
waiting in it (Limits).

**The excerpt.** Step 3 for the time step, in `MeshImpl::max_time_step`:

```cpp
op.reduceOp = c10d::ReduceOp::MIN;
if (layout->has_process_group()) layout->comm->allreduce(dt_reduce, op.reduceOp);
...
return pow(2., -redo) * cfl * dt;   // 2^{-n_redo} C dt
```

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- Signals are read only in `check_redo`, once per cycle. A rank that never reaches it (a hang elsewhere) never
  handles its signal, and the others wait in the collective; the comment in
  `CheckSignalFlags` {{< code src/utils/signal_handler.cpp SignalHandler::CheckSignalFlags >}} says so.
- Every collective is blocking and sits on the host, so each costs a device-to-host copy on GPU (@sec-ch14-gpu).
- The fixer SUM is a floating-point sum whose grouping changes with the decomposition (cells per block, blocks per
  process, process count) and whose order across processes is left to the backend; no test measures its effect
  (@sec-ch14-repro).
:::

<!-- reader glossary notes -->
[^rg-9793b59d7bc0]: $C$ — Courant number (named: acoustic, advective, vertical acoustic)

[^rg-fe505223b66c]: cfl — Courant-number limit for the time step

[^rg-abef336e38dd]: $\Theta$ — the positivity limiter's donor factor in $[0,1]$: the fraction of a requested face flux the limiter allows. Capital, because $\theta$ is the colatitude

[^rg-6f5d38ae36e6]: $\epsilon_{\mathrm{m}}$ — machine epsilon of the working precision (never bare $\epsilon$, which is $\epsilon_{\mathrm{piv}}$); [source](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/c0c38593d3d3f37bebe204a590610fd7daa05a5f/src/hydro/flux_positivity.cpp#L11-L14)

[^rg-0726addd7156]: VIC — vertically implicit correction

[^rg-e0adecef2ed5]: CFL — Courant–Friedrichs–Lewy

[^rg-9751aed7d553]: ncycle_out — number of cycles between printed cycle lines; 0 turns the line off
<!-- end reader glossary notes -->
